answer: The war that erupted in late February 2026 has produced a string of high‑profile attacks on energy sites across the Gulf. On 18 March 2026 Israeli missiles struck Iran’s South Pars gas‑field complex at Asaluyeh, igniting fires that forced several units offline. Two days earlier, on 16 March 2026, an Iranian drone hit the Shah natural‑gas field in the United Arab Emirates, prompting an immediate suspension of operations. Iranian drones also targeted oil refining capacity in Kuwait, setting fire to multiple units at the Mina Al‑Ahmadi refinery on 3 April 2026. The following week, on 5 April 2026, Gulf Petrochemical Industries in Bahrain suffered fires after a drone strike. In addition, Iranian ballistic missiles damaged two of the fourteen liquefaction trains at Qatar’s Ras Laffan LNG facility, with the hit trains expected to remain out of service for up to five years.
